question.problem:
$\,$ $x$ is prime and $x$ is odd.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(x\text{ is prime}\text{ and }x\text{ is odd}) & ≡¬((x\text{ is prime})∧(x\text{ is odd})) \\  & ≡¬(x\text{ is prime})∨¬(x\text{ is odd}) \\  & ≡(x\text{ is not prime})∨(x\text{ is even}) \\  & ≡x\text{ is not prime}\text{ or }x\text{ is even}.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: $x$ is not prime and $x$ is odd
$x$ is not prime or $x$ is odd
$x$ is not prime and $x$ is even
$x$ is not prime or $x$ is even
